title: How Much Fiber Per Day? Daily Targets + Calculator
description: How much fiber should you eat per day? See commonly cited U.S. Adequate Intake levels by sex and age, then estimate today’s intake with a free calculator.
h1: How much fiber should you eat per day?
intro: In the U.S., Adequate Intake for fiber is often summarized as about 14g per 1,000 calories. Everyday reference totals are commonly shown as ~25g/day for women 19–50, ~38g for men 19–50, and lower after age 50.

Those figures are population references, not a personal medical prescription. Fibermaxxing on this site means Standard × 1.5 (capped at 50g) as an optional stretch — increase gradually and drink water.
defaultMeal: I ate 2 eggs, 1 bowl of oatmeal, and an apple

faqs.q: What is the recommended fiber intake per day?
faqs.a: Commonly cited U.S. Adequate Intake examples: women 19–50 ≈ 25g; men 19–50 ≈ 38g; women 51+ ≈ 21g; men 51+ ≈ 30g. Individual needs vary with calories and health status.
Standard daily target × 1.5, capped at 50g. Not medical advice and not an official guideline.

faqs.q: How do I know how much I ate?
faqs.a: Paste your meals into the calculator for a USDA-based estimate, then edit portions if a match looks wrong.

title: Oatmeal Fiber Content (Cooked Cup) + Calculator
description: How much fiber is in oatmeal? About 4g per 1 cup cooked oatmeal in our USDA-based reference serving. Estimate a full day with the free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in oatmeal?
intro: Cooked oatmeal is one of the easiest high-fiber breakfast bases. Exact grams depend on dry vs cooked weight and add-ins (fruit, chia, nuts).
Use the reference below, then paste your full day — including the oatmeal bowl — to see progress toward your daily target.

facts.label: Cooked oatmeal
facts.note: Curated USDA-style reference on this site (Oatmeal, cooked)

facts.label: Dry rolled oats
facts.value: Higher per 100g; portions are smaller by volume
facts.note: Prefer logging “oatmeal” as prepared if that is what you ate

facts.label: Source
facts.note: See Method & Sources on this site

defaultMeal: 1 bowl of oatmeal with chia seeds and blueberries

faqs.q: How much fiber is in a cup of oatmeal?
faqs.a: On this site, cooked oatmeal is referenced around 4g fiber per 1 cup (234g). Brands and water ratios vary — edit grams after you calculate if needed.
Dry oats are denser per cup. If you ate a prepared bowl, log cooked oatmeal; if you weighed dry oats, prefer a grams amount.

faqs.q: How do I boost oatmeal fiber?
faqs.a: Common add-ins: chia or flax, berries, pear, beans at later meals. Recalculate the full day after changes.

title: Chia Seeds Fiber (per Tbsp) + Daily Calculator
description: Chia seeds have about 3.4g fiber per tablespoon (~10g) using USDA chia fiber density on this site. Estimate your full day with the free calculator.
h1: How much fiber is in chia seeds?
intro: Chia is fiber-dense: a tablespoon goes a long way. Our calculator scales from USDA chia fiber per 100g (about 34.4g fiber/100g).
Log chia pudding, smoothies, or sprinkled seeds with the rest of your meals, then adjust grams if your scoop differs.

facts.label: 1 tbsp chia (≈10g)
facts.note: From USDA Seeds, chia seeds, dried (34.4g fiber / 100g)

facts.label: 1 oz chia (28.35g)
facts.note: Default USDA portion label on this food row

defaultMeal: Chia pudding with raspberries and Greek yogurt

faqs.q: How much fiber is in a tablespoon of chia?
faqs.a: About 3.4g on this site when we treat 1 tbsp as ~10g of dried chia seeds. Edit grams after matching if your scale reading differs.
Psyllium is a concentrated husk; chia is a whole seed. Compare labels and your tolerance — then calculate real portions.

faqs.q: Can I only eat chia to hit my goal?
faqs.a: Usually better to mix legumes, grains, fruit, and vegetables. Chia is a strong helper, not the whole diet.

title: High Fiber Breakfast Ideas (with Portions) + Calculator
description: Three high-fiber breakfasts with item portions and approximate fiber totals (~9g, ~12g, ~10g), plus a free calculator for your own meal.
intro: A fiber-forward breakfast can remove a large share of the day’s gap early. Below are three combinations with reference portions and approximate fiber totals from this site’s USDA-based data.
Paste the oat-bowl example into the calculator (or type your own meal), then edit servings or grams. Totals change when portions change.

facts.label: Oat bowl · ~9g fiber
facts.value: 1 cup cooked oatmeal + 1 tbsp chia seeds + ½ cup blueberries

facts.label: Chia pudding · ~12g fiber
facts.value: 2 tbsp chia seeds + ½ cup raspberries + 170g Greek yogurt

facts.label: Savory plate · ~10g fiber
facts.value: ½ avocado + 1 slice whole-wheat bread + 1 medium orange
facts.note: ~5g + ~1.9g + ~3g (hand-referenced USDA lines; eggs add protein, not fiber)

defaultMeal: 1 cup oatmeal, 1 tbsp chia seeds, 1/2 cup blueberries

faqs.a: Examples include oatmeal with fruit and seeds, chia pudding, or whole-wheat toast with avocado and fruit — portions decide the gram total.
They sum this site’s USDA-based reference servings for the named portions (for example, 1 cup cooked oatmeal ≈ 4g). Brands and prep vary — recalculate after you edit grams.

faqs.q: How many grams should breakfast provide?
faqs.a: There is no official breakfast quota. Many people aim for a sizable fraction of their daily Adequate Intake early; use the calculator to see your split.
No — examples are pre-filled. Press Calculate fiber when you want results, then edit portions.
